newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel general says preparing for war with Syria.
newsitem.headline: Israel general says preparing for war with Syria.

text.p: Israel's deputy army chief of staff said on Thursday Israel was preparing for a possible war with Syria in 1997.
"The working estimate for 1997 is that we can find ourselves in a military confrontation with Syria," Deputy Chief of Staff Matan Vilnai told Israel's Channel One television.
"This year we are directing our training...in order to stand against the Syria army," Vilnai said, adding: "In a regular year I would say that is a waste."

Earlier this week Israel's air force intelligence chief said the probability of war with the Arabs could no longer be characterised as low and the Damascus remained "Israel's number one confrontation state".

Despite the war jitters, Israel's right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to make the peace with arch-foe Syria that evaded his left-leaning predecessors despite his refusal to give up the occupied Golan Heights.

Syria, demanding the return of the strategic plateau Israel seized in a 1967 war, has assailed Netanyahu for rejecting the land-for-peace policy of the dovish government he ousted in May and for backing Jewish settlement on the Golan.

Five years of sporadic peace talks between Israel and Syria over the fate of the plateau have yet to resume under Netanyahu. Instead of talking peace, the longtime enemies have heated up a war of words.
Israel's previous Labour party leaders the late Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres were prepared to make at least a partial pullback from the Golan in exchange for peace.
